In addition to providing public comment in person at the meeting, the following opportunity has been
established:

Public Comments
Please email all public comments to CScommission@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line
of your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business)
and Item Number you are commenting on. The Staff will read public comments into the record for up to
the three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.

   MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 7, 2022
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Huerta called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at 6:34
P.M. on Monday, November 7, 2022, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at
City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Cordero.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Cheryl Anne Cabot, Catherine Cordero, Theresa Huerta
  and Ting Xie
Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Supervisor Alatorre provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and how to
request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services Commission, email all
public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT
  George Young provided an update regarding the San Gabriel Sea Gulls swim team.
  The Sea Gulls held their Halloween meet recently and are still doing their normal
  activities.

  During public comment, it was brought to our attention that we were experiencing audio
  issues with the YouTube livestream.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 7, 2022
   A motion was made by Chair Huerta and seconded by Commission Cabot to take a
  short health break to give staff a time to investigate the issue.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CABOT, CORDERO, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

  The meeting resumed at 6:54 p.m. The Commission decided to continue to the meeting
  without a livestream.

  Andrew made a comment about diversity. He attended the October HEAR Commission
  and noticed there were 5 women and only 2 men. He commented that the Community
  Services Commission is comprised of all women, so he wanted to bring it to the
  commission’s attention. He is concerned there is not enough male representation.

3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot, seconded by Vice Chair Xie to
  approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for
  October 3, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CABOT, CORDERO, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. EMPLOYEE INTRODUCTION – DANIELLE ADRIANO
  Director Perez introduced the new Recreation Coordinator, Danielle Adriano.

  Public Comment: None

  B. YEAR IN-REVIEW
  This presentation was provided by Supervisor Alatorre, Supervisor Gomez-
  Cortez, Recreation Coordinator Adriano, and Manager Morales-Stevens.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 7, 2022
   The Commission had questions about the various programs the department
  offers. They asked if the older adult programs were only available for residents,
  which movies were shown at the senior days and if they could participate in the
  Health & Wellness Fair next year. The Commissioners were impressed by the
  number of activities and programs that were held throughout the year.

  Public Comment: None

  C. DISCUSSION OF 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN AND DEVELOP 2023
  WORKPLAN
  Supervisor Alatorre provided the update.

  The Commission expressed they would like to host a Community Services Day.
  They do not want to financially impact the city, so they would like to be present
  at family events with a booth. The Commission provided updates regarding
  their progress on the 2022 workplan items.

  Item 1 – Vice Chair Xie stated Item 1C will be on the 2023 workplan, she needs
  time to learn more about the translation services we offer.

  Item 2 – Chair Huerta will be meeting with the Herald Christian Center and
  would like to extend this item into 2023.

  Item 3 – Commission Cabot plans to hold the Moon Festival in 2023, she has
  been in communication with Mayor Ding and says he is very excited about this
  event.

  Item 4 – Commissioner Cordero and Commissioner Cabot have met with
  Manager Morales-Stevens and hope to schedule a tour of our parks with
  Assemblyman Fong, Senator Rubio and Congresswoman Hilda Solis. This item
  will also be moved to 2023.

  Item 5 – Vice Chair Xie shared she is waiting for information from staff and will
  plan a meeting with the city’s public information officer to discuss social media
  platforms. Item 5B will be moved to 2023.

  D. MONTHLY DEPARTMENT REPORT
  Supervisor Alatorre presented the report.

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 7, 2022
   Commissioner Cabot attended the Fall Fun Festival and was a judge for the
  costume contest. She said it was very well organized and complimented
  Recreation Leader, Cristhianee Sanchez, for being an excellent MC for the
  contest.

  Commissioner Cordero was also a judge for the costume contest at the Fall Fun
  Festival. In addition, she attended Dia de los Muertos.

  Vice Chair Xie was a judge for the costume contest at the Fall Fun Festival, she
  also took videos of all the booths and will create a collage. She said this event
  had a large turnout and is exactly what the community needed.

  Public Comment: None

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  A. DATES TO REMEMBER
  Supervisor Alatorre presented the item.

  Public Comment: None

  B. GENERAL STAFF COMMENTS
  Supervisor Alatorre presented the item.

  Public Comment: None

7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Huerta adjourned the meeting at 8:18 p.m.

  Next regular meeting held on Monday, December 5, 2022, in the Council Chamber
  at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, at 6:30 pm.

Respectfully submitted:

_____________________________________
Adrienne Franquez, Commission Clerk

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  December 5, 2022

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Youth Programs
After School Program – The After School Program at Coolidge, McKinley, Roosevelt,
Washington, and Wilson Elementary Schools are celebrating the holiday season with
festive arts and crafts, and letters to Santa.
Priority registration for the spring semester begins December 5 for all returning students.
Registration for new students begins December 12. Registration is available by calling the
Community Services Department.
Jefferson Middle School Sports – The Jefferson Middle School Boys and Girls Varsity, and
Boys Junior Varsity Basketball teams began games starting the week of November 28.
Games were played against Huntington, Oak and South Pasadena Middle Schools. The
Community Services Department Recreation Leaders/Coaches will be attending the
Southern California Municipal Athletic Federation’s (SCMAF) Scorers and Coaches
Training on December 17 to provide a higher level of game play for Jefferson Middle
School.

Older Adults
Holiday Lunch – On Monday, December 12 the senior holiday lunch will include holiday
festivities and old fashion carolers. Registration can be made by calling the Community
Services Office. Registration closes December 7.
Movie Days – On Monday, December 12 at 12:30pm the Adult Center will feature Miracle
on 34th Street (1947). This holiday movie will feature holiday treats.
Holiday Bingo – On Thursday, December 15 the Adult Center will host a holiday themed
Bingo. Register by calling the Community Services Department.
Table Tennis – Table tennis is now taking place at the Recreation Building Dance Room
on Thursdays from 8:00-11:00am and Friday’s from 1:30-5:30pm.

  4-A
 Trips – Registration is available for the trip to the Riverside Mission Inn festival of lights.
This trip will take place on December 13 and costs $40. Registration is available for the
trip to Long Beach for a luncheon and Beach Boys Tribute. This trip will take place on
December 18 and costs $90. Over the phone or in-person at the Community Services
Department.

Events
Turkey Trot – The 45th Annual Turkey Trot took place on Saturday, November 19 at
Vincent Lugo Park. There were 172 participants registered for the event. The event
included a 5K run and walk, 10K run, and a 1K kids run. Active SGV partnered with the city
to offer the Go-Human demonstration, a temporary high visibility crosswalk along the 1K
route in front of McKinley Elementary School.
Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony – The Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony will take place
on Tuesday, December 6. The event will include food trucks, refreshments, live
entertainment, ornament decorating and a tree lighting ceremony, followed by a visit
from Santa. Entertainment will be provided by the Dewey Elementary School, Community
Services dance classes, the Roosevelt Elementary School Orchestra and Concert Band.

  4-A
